description:
Evaluate and integrate OPA (Open Policy Agent) and Casbin for policy enforcement. Two distinct roles, no overlap.

## Casbin — Sieve capability enforcement
What actions is a given Sieve script layer allowed to perform? The four-layer capability model (system/domain/mailbox/user, each with different allowed actions, operator-configurable restrictions) is exactly Casbin's design target. Embed as library (casbin-rs). Policy defined in model file, not code.

## OPA — Mailbox access decisions
Replace or augment stoa's grant-check SQL query with OPA policy evaluation. Identity context (sub, trust_tier, active_providers, session_groups) + resource context (mailbox_id, requested_permission, min_trust_level) → allow/deny with reason. Policy lives in Rego files, version-controlled, deployed independently of stoa. Enables operators (DoD, GSA, LF, community) to have radically different access policies on the same stoa codebase.

## OPA deployment model
Prefer sidecar over embedded library. OPA is designed to run as a sidecar with a REST API. Decouples policy updates from stoa restarts — operator can push new Rego bundle without touching stoa. stoa calls OPA over HTTP if configured, falls back to built-in grant-check SQL if OPA not present. OPA is optional, never required.

## Rust ecosystem status at time of writing (2026-05)
OPA: regorus (Microsoft's Rego evaluator in Rust) exists and is actively maintained, used in Azure, but not battle-hardened at OPA scale. opa-wasm also exists. Neither is mature enough to embed confidently yet — sidecar preferred.
Casbin: casbin-rs is reasonably mature.

## Integration points
Casbin → crates/sieve-native: capability check before evaluating each action in script
OPA → crates/mail + crates/smtp: access decision on every mailbox grant check, JMAP request, SMTP RCPT TO

## Revisit when
regorus matures sufficiently for production embedding, OR a customer requires OPA integration, OR Casbin-rs proves insufficient for capability model complexity.
title: design: OPA and Casbin integration for policy enforcement
